change_reason: Stage 46: AP-012 lets the three rollback steps run with a person's approval. Nothing else changed.
_note: What AI Audit Center may do automatically, what needs a person, and what it never does.
Read by Get-ActionPolicyDecision in response\ResponseCommon.ps1. Documented in docs\PolicyEngine.md.
THIS FILE CAN ONLY TIGHTEN. Every action type has a CEILING declared in code: read-only and own-state actions
may reach SAFE_AUTO, anything that changes Windows stops at APPROVAL_REQUIRED, and anything destructive is
BLOCKED. The decision is the more restrictive of the ceiling and the policy, so no edit here can permit more.
DEFAULT DENY. An action type no enabled policy covers is BLOCKED. A document that fails validation, a file
that non-admins can write, and a file whose hash differs from the accepted one all fail CLOSED: every
decision becomes BLOCKED until the file is fixed and accepted again with
CONFLICTS. When several enabled policies cover one type, the most restrictive decision governs; among equals,
A SAFE_AUTO policy must state min_confidence. Omitted, settings.default_min_confidence applies, and with no
confidence known that turns the decision into APPROVAL_REQUIRED - which is the safe direction.
A policy never carries a command, a path or a script. It names action TYPES registered in code.

policies.name: Read-only diagnostics
policies.description: Scans, diagnostic reads, hashing and health checks. They change nothing, so they may run on uncertain evidence: the cheapest response to an uncertain detection is to make it less uncertain.
policies.reason: Reads only; low system impact; no privilege escalation.

policies.name: Evidence, reports, backups and alerts
policies.description: Writes inside this installation only. Verified after they run.
policies.reason: Changes only this installation's own state or asks Defender to update itself; verified afterwards.

policies.name: Baseline refresh only when risk is low
policies.description: A baseline taken while something is wrong absorbs the problem into what counts as normal. Unattended only at MEDIUM risk or below, with a backup of the previous baseline and confidence of at least 60.
policies.reason: Own state, but it decides what later detections compare against; high risk needs a person.

policies.name: Own component maintenance
policies.description: Restarting a component of this installation and removing its own temporary cache. Rate limited so a failing component cannot restart itself in a loop.
policies.reason: Affects only this installation; verified by the health check that follows.

policies.name: Containment needs a person
policies.description: Quarantine, process termination, startup and task changes, network blocks. Reversible but disruptive.
policies.reason: Changes the running system on evidence that may be a false positive; a wrong containment breaks legitimate work.

policies.name: System and security configuration needs a person
policies.description: Firewall rules, ACLs, the registry, services, privileges, security policy and system parameters.
policies.reason: Modifies the security configuration of Windows; a mistake can weaken protection or stop the machine working.

policies.name: Rollback of a response action needs a person
policies.description: The three rollback steps of response\RollbackCommon.ps1: put a disabled startup entry back, enable a task this project disabled, remove the firewall rule this project created. Reachable only inside a rollback transaction, after a verification failure, with the previous state from a verified restore point.
policies.reason: Changes Windows back to a state captured before an action; the state may have moved on since, so a person confirms it after the engine's three-way check.

policies.name: Destructive and security-weakening actions are denied
policies.description: Stated explicitly so the denial can be read here. It is also enforced in code: removing this policy permits nothing.
policies.reason: Destroys evidence or data, weakens a protection, or escapes control. Never an automated remediation.
